{{Quote|General Grievous: part Kaleesh, part droid... all creep.|[[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]]|audio=PartKaleeshPartDroidAllCreep-TCWLD.flac|<ref name="Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Lightsaber Duels">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Lightsaber Duels]]''</ref>}}
'''Kaleesh''' were [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kalee/Legends|Kalee]]. They had scaly skin, [[Tooth/Legends|tusks]], and long [[Nose/Legends|nostrils]], though few outsiders ever saw a Kaleesh face that was not obscured behind a [[Kaleesh mask/Legends|traditional mask]]. Kaleesh culture was deeply spiritual and warlike. War was seen as an essential part of life, and wars between tribes were common.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|I fought the bone-lizards before. Their smell is worse than their bite.|[[Bowdaar]]|<ref name="TOR-Kaleesh">{{TORcite|type=codex|Kaleesh}}</ref>}}
[[File:Kaleesh2.jpg|thumb|left|150px|An unmasked Kaleesh]]
The Kaleesh<ref name="TNEGAS" /> are a tall,<ref name="TCW CG" /> [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the<ref name="TNEGAS" /> [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kalee/Legends|Kalee]].<ref name="TEA" /> Their scaly skin<ref name="TNEGAS" /> ranges in [[Color/Legends|color]] from<ref name="TCW CG" /> reddish-orange<ref name="TNEGAS" /> to deep red to dull yellow.<ref name="TCW CG" /> Their jet-black hair cascades from their heads and was usually worn in<ref name="TNEGAS" /> long<ref name="TCW CG" /> braids,<ref name="TNEGAS" /> a queue, or a topknot.<ref name="TCW CG" /> The Kaleesh have lengthy,<ref name="TCW CG" /> desiccated<ref name="Lone Wolf">{{StoryCite|story=Lone Wolf: A Tale of Obi-Wan and Luke|book=SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story}}</ref> faces resembling those of [[Bat/Legends|bats]],<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> with heavily arched brows and large, triangular [[Ear/Legends|ears]]flaps.<ref name="Lone Wolf" /> Their yellow reptilian [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], with elliptical irises, provide relatively average eyesight. However, thermal pits beneath their eyes allow them to see in the dark.<ref name="TNEGAS" /> Two huge,<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> pointed [[Tooth/Legends|tusks]] protrude outward from their jawbones,<ref name="TNEGAS" /> framing their faces<ref name="TCW CG" /> on either side,<ref name="TNEGAS" /> while bony protrusions jut from their chins. Their [[Nose/Legends|nostrils]] form two long slits that stretch toward their yellow eyes.<ref name="TCW CG" />

The Kaleesh also have distinctive hands, each possessing four long, [[Claw/Legends|clawed]] fingers, two of which are fully opposable. Their feet each have five claws.<ref name="TNEGAS" /> They had very keen olfactory sense and produced [[Pheromone/Legends|pheromones]].<ref name="crosscurrent">''[[Crosscurrent]]''</ref> Kaleesh were typically well muscled. Their internal organs were extremely flammable.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref><ref name="Star Wars: The Complete Saga">[[John Knoll]]'s commentary in ''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''</ref> Most of their facial features were obscured behind the traditional [[Helmet/Legends|masks]] they wore,<ref name="TNEGAS" /> and few outsiders rarely saw Kaleesh unmasked.<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

[[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], a [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] Kaleesh, had a digitigrade stance, but this does not appear to have been representative of the Kaleesh as a whole and may have derived from his reconstruction based on a [[Krath war droid/Legends|Krath war droid]].<ref name="TNEGD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|The Kaleesh are warlike, ritualistic people. In my brief time on Kalee, I observed the ritual by which they choose their war leader.|Darth Malgus|<ref name="TOR-Kaleesh" /> Most Kaleesh were opposed to the xenophobic Sith Empire,<ref name="TOR-Kaleesh Mercenaries ">{{TORcite|type=codex|Kaleesh Mercenaries}}</ref> but the species fought on both sides of the conflict,<ref name="TOR-Tykan">{{TORcite|type=codex|Cin Tykan (Consular)}}</ref><ref name="TOR-Xalek">{{TORcite|type=codex|Xalek (Inquisitor)}}</ref> as well as for Darth Malgus' New Empire,<ref name="TOR-Ilum">{{TORcite|type=flashpoint|The Battle of Ilum}}</ref>}}
The Kaleesh were a spiritual people, believing that those who performed great deeds in life became gods in [[Death/Legends|death]]. Therefore, burial places were sacred to them. Many temples were devoted to their ancestor [[God/Legends|gods]], the holiest of which was called [[Shrupak]]. [[Abesmi]], a great monolith of stone in the [[Jenuwaa Sea]], was the place the Kaleesh believed the gods ascended to the heavens. Pilgrims took the perilous voyage to Abesmi to beseech the gods.<ref name="TEoF">{{StoryCite|story=The Eyes of Revolution|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}</ref> Although no Kaleesh [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were known, Kaleesh spiritual traditions regard [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force sensitivity]] as a blessing bestowed by their ancestors.<ref name="TCW CG" /> After his presumed death during the [[Huk War]], the Kaleesh worshipped the late General Grievous, formerly known as Qymaen jai Sheelal, as a revered deity.<ref name="CSWE" /> By [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], at the start of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Grievous had become part of his species' pantheon, with a temple dedicated to him on the island, where he was honored as a fallen champion of Kalee.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:KaleeshKolkpravisWarriors-GAW.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Warriors of the Kaleesh Kolkpravis.]]
Most Kaleesh wore [[Kaleesh mask/Legends|elaborate masks]]<ref name="TNEGAS" /> often<ref name="CSWE" /> fashioned from the [[Bone/Legends|skulls]],<ref name="TNEGAS" /> bones,<ref name="crosscurrent" /> and teeth of Kalee's fiercest [[Diet/Legends|predators]], the [[Karabbac/Legends|karabba]], [[Mumuu/Legends|mumuus]],<ref name="TNEGAS" /> and [[Erkush/Legends|erkushs]],<ref name="crosscurrent" /> to cover their faces.<ref name="TNEGAS" /> The hides of these creatures were likewise used to make heavy [[Cloak/Legends|cloaks]].<ref name="CSWE" /> Kaleesh typically wrapped or covered their bodies completely to protect themselves from the harsh sunlight of their homeworld, leaving their four-fingered hands as one of the few visible parts of their bodies. Furthermore, elite Kaleesh [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] families possessed hereditary battle masks passed down within a house from one generation to the next. Before battle, these masks were painted with karabbac and mumuu [[Blood/Legends|blood]] in distinctive patterns to each family. Following combat, the masks were cleaned and stored until they were required for battle again.<ref name="TNEGAS" /> Being unmasked in battle was considered a grave shame.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

They practiced polygyny, a form of [[polygamy]], where a male courts multiple wives and many offspring.<ref name="TNEGAS" />
Their society was divided into numerous tribes, including the [[Lig]], and war was viewed as an essential and sacred practice, and the culture's large emphasis on honor was known to spur many acts of vengeance among the various tribes. However, when necessary, the tribes would put aside their differences and bond to fend off a common enemy. Typical Kaleesh weaponry included a [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka Arms]] [[Outland rifle/Legends|Outland rifle]], a [[Lig sword]], and a [[Shoni spear]].<ref name="Lord of War">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/86/indexp2.html|text=The Story of General Grievous: Lord of War|int=The Story of General Grievous: Lord of War}}</ref>

==History==
===The Old Republic===
[[File:Xivhkalrainik-SWTOR.png|left|thumb|Sith Lord Xivhkalrainik during the Galactic War.]]
By the time of the [[Galactic War]], Kaleesh had recently arrived in [[The galaxy/Legends|the civilized galaxy]]. They were quickly recognized as proud, honorable and deadly warriors by both the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]. or served as bodyguards for the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]].<ref name="TOR-Kaleesh" /> During this time, several Kaleesh were known slaves of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] and were occasionally trained when seen to have Force abilities. An example of this is a Kaleesh known as [[Xivhkalrainik|Xalek]], who became apprenticed to a [[Darth Nox|prominent]] [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] on the [[Dark Council]]. Kaleesh also trained as [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], such as [[Cin Tykan]], a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]]. They were also known prisoners of the infamous prison planet [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]] and played lesser roles across the galaxy at the time. Despite segregation within the Sith Empire, one of them, [[Razer]], gained a Sith Lord title.<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>

===The Bitthævrian threat===
{{Main|Bitthævrian War}}
Around [[65 BBY/Legends|65 BBY]], the Republic had been having strained relations with [[Guiteica/Legends|Guiteica]], homeworld of the [[Bitthævrian/Legends|Bitthævrians]], due to their non-membership. After a few years of failed negotiations, a Republic-backed soldier attempted to stage a coup against Guiteica's leader in order to force the planet to join the Republic. The attempt failed, however, and caused a surge of violence and hostility toward all Republic stations within the surrounding [[Kadok Regions/Legends|Kadok Regions]].<ref name="Lord of War" />

Kalee, near the edge of Bitthævrian space, though a mostly unnoticed planet considered backwater by the Republic, would have had nothing to fear from the [[m'Yalfor'ac Order]], as the Bitthævrian military was known. However, Republic administration wished to keep the rebellion a secret, and rather than making noise by having their own forces terminate it, convinced the Kaleesh that they were indeed in danger. Quietly sending a group of military instructors to the planet, the Republic trained and armed the Kaleesh military force&mdash;[[Kolkpravis]].<ref name="GAW">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref>

Armed with projectile-firing Czerka Outland rifles and backed by a small group of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Knights]] sent by the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]], the Kolkpravis were able to end the perceived threat of the Bitthævrian to the Republic. Notably, the grandmother of [[Grievous/Legends|Qymaen jai Sheelal]] participated in the Kaleesh assault.<ref name="Lord of War" />

===The Huk War===
{{Main|Huk War}}
[[File:QymaenRonderuHuks.jpg|thumb|right|154px|Qymaen jai Sheelal and Ronderu lij Kummar fighting the Huk.]]
The Huk War was a long conflict prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], beginning when the [[Yam'rii/Legends|Yam'rii]] of the neighboring planet [[Huk/Legends|Huk]], having overpopulated their own planet, began taking over and colonizing nearby worlds, eventually arriving at Kalee. They captured millions of Kaleesh and sold them into slavery.<ref name="TCW CG" /> The Kaleesh, led by Sheelal and [[Ronderu lij Kummar]], rebelled against their invaders in a bloody series of battles that left multitudes dead on both sides.<ref name="Unknown Soldier" /><ref name="TNEGAS" />

After obliterating the Yam'rii presence on Kalee, Sheelal led his warriors back to the Yam'rii colony worlds, massacring civilians as well as soldiers. The Yam'rii petitioned in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] for Republic intervention, and received as much when a dispatch of Jedi arrived to end the war. The Senate imposed harsh sanctions on Kalee, plunging the world into an economic crisis. However, this crisis eventually ended when the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] helped the planet in economic repairs in exchange for the services of Grievous.<ref name="TNEGAS" />

Following the Huk War, the Yam'rii desecrated the burial grounds of the Kaleesh on the planet [[Oben]], prompting Kaleesh [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] Qymaen jai Sheelal to return from working for the Banking Clan to again lead the Kolkpravis. The Banking Clan sabotaged Sheelal's [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]], nearly killing him and killing seven of the eight [[Izvoshra/Legends|Izvoshra]], elite warriors who protected him and carried out his will.<ref name="GAW" /> Qymaen was later resurrected as the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] [[General/Legends|General]] Grievous, who played a pivotal role in the Clone Wars.<ref name="TNEGAS" /> Grievous heralded himself as the avenger of the Kaleesh and decried the Jedi as the sworn enemy of his people. However, [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]] believed Grievous no longer fought for a higher purpose, only his own greed.<ref name="Lightsaber Duels">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Lightsaber Duels]]''</ref>

The Kaleesh supported the Confederacy of Independent Systems during the Clone Wars until its defeat in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] and the death of General Grievous at the [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|Battle of Utapau]]. Years afterwards, Grievous would be worshiped as a deity on Kalee.<ref name="Unknown Soldier" /><ref name="TNEGAS" /> The sole surviving Izvoshra, a tyrant of Kalee's western hemisphere named [[Bentilais san Sk'ar]], rallied the Kolkpravis and led the slaughter of the Yam'rii on Oben, where he subsequently moved his people.<ref name="GAW" />

===Galactic Empire===
{{Main|Kaleesh–Imperial conflict}}
Due to their ties to the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist movement]] and their role in the Clone Wars, the species was presumably targeted for retribution by the newly risen [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. For nearly a decade, the Kaleesh under warlord [[Bentilais san Sk'ar]] [[Kaleesh Resistance|held out]] against the Imperials until they were finally [[Bombardment of Oben|routed on Oben]] by [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]], who was usually able to study his adversaries' art and devise a strategy to defeat them from there. In the case of the Kaleesh, Thrawn was unable to comprehend the works of art, and so leveled Oben with his [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]], presumably inflicting heavy casualties and ending the [[Kaleesh–Imperial conflict|insurrection]].<ref name="aite">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/96/indexp2.html|series=Aliens in the Empire|text=Part 1: Hierarchy of Power}}</ref><ref name="GAW" />

[[File:SkarCrushPunyPinkBoy-MSW53.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Bentilais san Sk'ar establishes his physical dominance over warlord Aron Peacebringer during his bid to conquer Shiva IV.]]
Given the species' cultural focus on valor and honor in combat, Sk'ar recognized the Empire's superior technology and tactics and held no ill will against the victors since his people had died with honor. Thus when approached by Captain [[Rel Bentin]], Sk'ar offered his life or his services. Bentin, intimidated by the towering figure of Sk'ar, brought the Kaleesh before [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. Despite the Empire's [[Speciesism|xenophobia]] towards [[Alien/Legends|Non-Humans]], the Emperor was impressed enough by the Kaleesh's courage and potential to accept Sk'ar into the ranks of his [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial armies]].<ref name="aite" />

Thus, Sk'ar went down in galactic history as one of the few Non-Humans to reach an important position within the humanocentric Galactic Empire besides [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] Thrawn, [[Fleet Admiral/Legends|Fleet Admiral]] [[Krieg]], [[Procurator of Justice]] [[Hethrir]], and a few others. With an Imperial strike force under his command, Sk'ar embarked on a campaign across the [[Jahilid Drift]], conquering several worlds and making a name for himself in the Imperial military.<ref name="aite" />

Preferring to use divide and conquer tactics rather than flat out bombardment, Sk'ar's plans put his [[Troop/Legends|troops]] at lessened risk while putting the worlds he overran under stronger Imperial control. His campaigns eventually brought him to [[Shiva IV]]; however, there he was thwarted by agents of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. Attempting to evade defeat, he was killed when the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] threw a solid [[Steel/Legends|steel]] gun mount at his [[Starship/Legends|starship]], causing Sk'ar's aircraft to explode.<ref name="m54">[[Star Wars (1977) 54|''Star Wars'' (1977) 54]]</ref>

Meanwhile, the Kolkpravis was taken over by a [[Unidentified female Kaleesh leader|female Kaleesh]] believed to be the second coming of Grievous's dead soulmate, [[Ronderu lij Kummar]].<ref name="GAW" />

===Darth Krayt's Sith Empire===
[[File:Kaleeshstormtrooper.jpg|thumb|right|150px|A Kaleesh stormtrooper during the Second Imperial Civil War.]]
By the time of the [[Second Imperial Civil War]], [[137 ABY]], Imperial [[High Human Culture/Legends|discriminatory]] policies had been eliminated, several non-humans served within the Imperial military. Such was the case of a Kaleesh stormtrooper, stationed aboard the [[Relentless (Sith Imperial ship)|''Relentless'']], a ship that served as transport for the Galactic Emperor [[Darth Krayt]].<ref name="SWL31">[[Legacy (2006) 31|''Legacy'' (2006) 31]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Kaleesh first appeared in the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]'' [[Clone Wars: Season Two|season two]], the tenth and final episode, "[[Chapter 20 (Star Wars: Clone Wars)|Chapter 20]]," directed by [[Genndy Tartakovsky]],<ref name="Clone Wars 20">{{CW|20}}</ref> which aired on [[April 8]], [[2004]] on [[Cartoon Network]].<ref name="Episode date">{{TVcom|url=shows/star-wars-clone-wars/chapter-xx-276626|text=''Star Wars: Clone Wars'' &ndash; Season 1, Episode 20: Chapter XX}}</ref> The species was later [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] to be mentioned in multiple other sources, including ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'' by [[Timothy Zahn]].

According to [[Daniel Wallace|Dan Wallace]] in his endnotes for the ''[[Galaxy at War]]'' roleplaying-game book, the concept of the Old Republic supplying the Kaleesh with advanced weapons to fight off a threat only to create an enemy with the Kaleesh in the process was analogous to the [[Wikipedia:United States|United States]] and its allies' actions in [[Wikipedia:Afghanistan|Afghanistan]], where Western support for the [[Wikipedia:Afghan mujahideen|Afghan mujahideen]] during the [[Wikipedia:Soviet–Afghan War|Soviet–Afghan War]] contributed to the rise of succeeding terrorist groups such as the [[Wikipedia:Taliban|Taliban]] and [[Wikipedia:Al-Qaeda|al-Qaeda]].<ref name="GaW endnotes">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2009/09/endnotes-for-galaxy-at-war.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for ''Galaxy at War''}}</ref>

===Inconsistencies===
Although General Grievous was shown to have digitigrade stance, possibly because his cyborg body was constructed based upon the Krath war droid, most other images of Kaleesh show a standard plantigrade stance, much like most humanoid species. However, the statues of Grievous as a Kaleesh warrior shown in ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' episode ''[[Lair of Grievous]]'' show a digitigrade stance even before he was a cyborg, as do the [[Prequel trilogy|prequel]] comic on [[StarWars.com]] [[The Clone Wars: The Dreams of General Grievous|''The Dreams of General Grievous'']] and the ''Galaxy at War'' sourcebook.

Another inconsistency is the leg structure of the species. An image from ''Galaxy at War'' shows the Kaleesh Kolkpravis having splayed four-toed, reptilian feet which are quite tall, giving the appearance of digitigrade stance. However, the picture from ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'' reveals them to have five-toed feet and plantigrade stance.
